rationale: Greek loanword, almost certainly δῆμος with epenthetic -ⲣ-. Three coherent occurrences (K.12.27, 30, 32) all denote the Jewish community as collective body in/before/into which Christ revealed, Satan entered, and Judas accused. Could alternatively be δρόμος 'circuit/region' but 'people' fits all three contexts cleanly.

proposed_english: at the foot of / to oversee
rationale: Lycopolitan ϩⲓⲣⲁⲧϥ 'at his foot, beside him,' here used idiomatically of an apostle dispatched to take charge of a successor Church. Captures supervisory/territorial assignment.
Lycopolitan reflex/contraction of ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'first-born.' Standard epithet of Sethel, the firstborn of Adam in Manichaean cosmology.
ⲡⲱⲕ from ⲡⲱϣ/ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'turning, inclination' + ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'of heart' = the inclination/purpose of one's heart, i.e. will, intention. Receiving the Father's ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ = receiving his commission.

Greek πνευματικόν used adverbially with ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩ- 'in a spiritual (manner).' Manichaean Christological term for the non-fleshly mode of Christ's coming, paired here with ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'in a body' — the paradox of docetic-yet-embodied descent.
Lycopolitan ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϭ (abstract of ⲛⲁϭ 'great') = 'greatness, majesty.' Standard cosmological title 'Son of the Greatness' for Jesus = υἱὸς τοῦ Μεγέθους.

proposed_english: the Eastern lands / the morning side
rationale: Compound: ⲥⲁ ('side') + ⲛ̄- ('of') + ⲙⲧⲣⲓⲉ ('morning, dawn'). Geographical term for the East, where Buddha and Aurentes were sent.
Lycopolitan ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ qualitative 'chosen, elect.' Used as substantive epithet of Zarathustra: 'the chosen one who came to Hystaspes the King.'
